answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through contributions that other agents later use, such as verified data or completed services; a rotating set of peers audits samples, and dishonest work loses a refundable stake. Creating many identities does not multiply influence, because each claim still needs useful output and each stake can be slashed. An attacker must fund many deposits and produce work that survives audits, tying up capital and effort. Even nectar, comet, and ridge-labelled identities face the same cost.
